mekayis.metin: (قَزَمَ) الْقَافُ وَالزَّاءُ وَالْمِيمُ كَلِمَةٌ تَدُلُّ عَلَى دَنَاءَةٍ وَلُؤْمٍ. فَالْقَزَمُ: الدَّنَاءَةُ وَاللُّؤْمُ. وَالرَّجُلُ قَزَمٌ، يُقَالُ ذَلِكَ لِلْأُنْثَى وَالذَّكَرِ، وَالْوَاحِدِ وَالْجَمْعِ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.t:
Etymology tree
Ottoman Turkish قازمق (kazmak)
Ottoman Turkish قازمه (kazma)der.
Arabic قزم
From Ottoman Turkish قازمه (kazma, “pickaxe”), from Ottoman Turkish قازمق (kazmak, “to dig out, to excavate”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kaŕ- (“to dig out”). From the common cross-cultural depictions of dwarves working the earth, likely bolstered by the real-life use of smaller individuals in mines to reach inaccessible places.
s: Ottoman Turkish قازمق (kazmak, “to dig out, to excavate”)
g: someone of baser lineage, low class
